claims.text: The feedstock is homogeneous gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder sieved to 10–60 μm and dispersed in an acrylate photocurable resin.
The green bodies are produced by DLP using a 405 nm source at 19.57 mW/cm², 100 s exposure per 70 μm layer, and 20 layers.
Continuous mechanical-pump evacuation during debinding creates an oxygen-deficient environment.
Oxygen-deficient debinding retains carbon in regions formerly occupied by the photocurable resin.
Retained carbon reduces pore volume in the debound or sintered component.
Incomplete oxidation under oxygen-deficient conditions reduces the rapid generation and escape of CO and CO₂.
Reduced gas evolution minimizes pressure-driven surface and interlayer cracking.
Oxygen-deficient debinding suppresses detrimental surface oxide layers that would otherwise hinder interparticle mass transport.
Reduced oxide formation and gas evolution enhance diffusion, interfacial bonding, and densification.
Oxygen-deficient debinding accelerates the disappearance of the DLP layered morphology.
Retaining carbon through oxygen-deficient debinding reduces residual thermal stresses.
Ambient-air-debound specimens require 24 h sintering at 1100 °C for full consolidation.
Ambient-air-debound specimens sintered at 1100 °C have approximately 5.1 MPa compressive strength.
Ambient-air-debound specimens exhibit prominent cracking caused by rapid gas evolution.
Oxygen-deficient debinding will enable full consolidation at about 1050 °C, approximately 50 °C below the ambient-air baseline.
At about 1050 °C, oxygen-deficient specimens will attain compressive strength comparable to ambient-air specimens sintered at 1100 °C.
Oxygen-deficient specimens will have less surface cracking and better interparticle bonding than the ambient-air baseline.
At sintering temperatures significantly below 1000 °C, elemental diffusion may be insufficient for full consolidation.
At temperatures above 1100 °C, stripe-like precipitates may form.
